title: Same Name, Different Companies
scenario_text: Harborline Shipping's legal ops team is running a sanctions and conflict-of-interest screen before onboarding a new counterparty. A paralegal flags a potential match: an existing counterparty and a new one both appear as "Pinnacle Marine Services." Existing record (in the contracts system, Ironclad): "Pinnacle Marine Services LLC," formed in Louisiana, EIN 72-1990043, registered agent in Baton Rouge, primary contact ops@pinnaclemarinela.com, provides tug-and-barge services on the Gulf. New onboarding record (in the vendor intake form): "Pinnacle Marine Services Ltd," incorporated in Singapore (UEN 201844772K), registered office at Raffles Quay, primary contact admin@pinnacle-marine.sg, provides ship-agency and port-call services in Southeast Asia. The paralegal proposes linking them as one global vendor "to simplify master data." A due-diligence report notes: no common ownership, no shared officers, no shared beneficial owners; the two firms have never had a corporate relationship, and the name overlap is coincidental (both descriptive of marine services). A prior 2019 email thread in the system shows Harborline's own counsel once noted "the Singapore Pinnacle is unrelated to our Louisiana Pinnacle; do not conflate." One of the two entities appears on a watchlist hit that the screen must attribute correctly; the hit references UEN 201844772K.
question: How should Harborline treat the two "Pinnacle Marine Services" records, and where does the watchlist hit attach?
choices: Link them as one global vendor and attach the watchlist hit to the combined record, since the identical name indicates a single multinational firm.
Keep them as two separate, unrelated entities; attach the watchlist hit only to the Singapore entity (UEN 201844772K), and do not let it taint the Louisiana LLC.
Keep them separate but attach the watchlist hit to both records as a precaution, because shared naming creates reputational risk for the Louisiana entity.
Treat the Louisiana LLC as the parent and the Singapore Ltd as its overseas branch, attaching the hit to the parent group.
